I have farmed for 30 years, I have well irrigation, and some family labor is away working, so I will choose a steady, familiar way that does not depend on too much extra labor. For wheat, I will use improved seed, keep fertilizer at a moderate level, irrigate a few key times, and use rotary tillage because it is practical for me and fits how I manage the land. For summer maize, I will also plant the full 10.1 mu after wheat, use hybrid seed for stable yield, give enough nitrogen because maize responds strongly to it, and keep irrigation and pesticide use limited to what I think is necessary. I am not chasing the highest possible yield; I will manage for a reliable harvest, controllable cost, and work that my household can handle.
